transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

E:15 on your Bosch means: Water-protection (anti-flood) system activated - water in base pan; drain pump runs, cycle locked (close tap). From what you have described, the most likely cause is door seal / gasket. Can you tell me whether water escapes from the SIDE or EDGE of the door during washing?
No water on the kitchen floor at all, and the door seal looks okay to me. I can see a little shine of water in the base tray through a gap by the plinth though.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is damaged / split spray arm firing water at the door. Can you tell me whether a leak at the door only during washing AND a split, cracked or obstructed lower spray arm?

I can't see any leak at the door, there's no water on the floor at all. I can't pull the unit out to check the spray arm area underneath either, it's fully integrated under the worktop. What else could it be?

It could be a faulty water level sensor or a control board issue causing the pump to run continuously. It might also be a hidden leak into the base tray that is triggering the safety switch despite no visible floor water. From what you have described, the most likely cause is is there water in the base, and where is it leaking from (find the source first). Can you tell me whether the drain pump keeps running with an empty tub?

Yes, the pump hums constantly while E:15 is showing. I haven't looked at whether the tub is empty, so I'm not sure about that. The only water I can see is that bit of shine in the base tray through the gap by the plinth.

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is drain filter (twist out and clean - first thing). Take out the lower rack, then twist and lift out the filter in the bottom of the tub. Rinse it under the tap and clear any food, grease or glass from the sump underneath. Was the filter or sump blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
I did the filter already and it was fairly clean. Plug is in the cupboard behind the unit so I can't easily unplug it, but I can switch it off at the isolator. What next?

You should switch off the power at the isolator to stop the pump and prevent damage. Then, carefully pull the dishwasher out from under the worktop to access the base tray and check for standing water or a blocked drain hose. From what you have described, the most likely cause is is there water in the base, and where is it leaking from (find the source first). Tall trays or items hanging below the lower rack can deflect the spray straight at the door seal. With the racks loaded, turn each spray arm by hand. Was anything catching the arms or pointing at the door (and have you moved it), or is everything clear?

I can't pull the unit out, it's fitted under the worktop and the plinth is glued. I've not noticed anything catching the spray arms, but I can't see under them. Is there anything else I can try without moving it, or is this an engineer job?

Since you have already cleaned the filter and confirmed no water is on the floor, the persistent E:15 code with a humming pump indicates a likely internal blockage or sensor fault that cannot be safely resolved from the outside. You should switch off the power at the isolator and contact an engineer to diagnose the issue without moving the unit. From what you have described, the most likely cause is filter / sump / impeller blockage (clear first). Next: Clear the filter, sump and impeller of debris. Let me know what you find.
